q: 1. Two projects having the same status expect payback period which project will be selected?
options: The project having more payback period
The project having less payback period
All off all of the above
explain: If everything else is equal, the project that recovers its investment sooner (shorter payback period) is preferred because it carries less risk and returns cash faster.

q: 2. The number of years required for the net operating benefit to pay back the initial cost of project is called ......
explain: This is the definition of payback period: years needed for net operating benefits to recover the initial cost.

q: 3. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be ......
explain: The minimum (threshold) B/C ratio is 1, where benefits just equal costs. Note: strictly, B/C above 1 is preferred; the key gives the threshold value.

q: 4. For the selection of any project the NPV should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable if NPV is zero or more; the minimum acceptable NPV is 0. A negative NPV is rejected, so option b cannot be right.

q: 5. If NPV is +ve then, NFV is ......
explain: NFV = NPV x (1+i)^n, and (1+i)^n is always positive, so NFV has the same sign as NPV.

q: 6. The ratio of discounted benefit and discounted cost is called
explain: This defines the Benefit-Cost ratio.

q: 7. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be
explain: The decision threshold is exactly 1.

q: 8. For selection of the project net present value should be ......
explain: A project is selected when its NPV is positive, meaning benefits exceed costs.

q: 9. For accepting of project, the minimum value of benefit cost ratio should be
explain: For a project to be minimally acceptable, BCR must be at least equal to one (benefits at least cover costs).

q: 10. The numerical value of MARR is
explain: For a project to be accepted, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) must exceed the MARR.

q: 11. For the selection of any project the NPV should be
explain: Per the answer key, the minimum acceptable NPV threshold for project selection is zero (NPV ≥ 0 indicates the project is at least break-even in present value terms).

q: 12. MARR (Marginal annual rate of return) is
explain: MARR represents the minimum acceptable rate of return expected as benefit resulting after an investment is made (note: options a and b are printed identically in the source book).

q: 13. Find the NPV if initial investment 5,000, Benefit for three years = 3000 per year and discount rate = 9%.
14. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be confirmly rejected?
explain: Any project with a negative NPV (-1) fails to meet the minimum required rate of return and should be rejected.

q: 15. In FW method, the minimum condition which the project is feasible is
explain: Similar to PW, the Future Worth (FW) must be positive (or zero) for a project to be economically justified.

q: 16. Which of the following has least significance in Benefit cost Analysis of a public project?
options: identification of relevant benefits and costs
measurement of the benefits and costs
explain: In benefit-cost analysis of public projects, payback period is of least significance compared to properly identifying, measuring, and handling uncertainty in benefits and costs.

q: 17. During calculation of IRR, NPV should be
explain: The Internal Rate of Return is defined mathematically as the discount rate that makes the NPV exactly zero.

q: 18. In any study the details of project are given below: Project a1=10.8%, a2=15.8%, a3=11%. Which project will be selected?
explain: The project with the highest Internal Rate of Return (15.8%) is the most economically attractive choice.

q: 19. Net Present Value (NPV) is defined as the total present value (PV) of .......of cash flows:
explain: NPV is defined as the total present value of the net amount of cash flows (inflows minus outflows) over the project's life.

q: 20. A project is said to be feasible when its net present value (NPV) is
explain: Per the answer key, a project is considered feasible when its NPV is greater than one (i.e., positive/greater than the threshold value).

q: 21. Which of the following is true for the present worth method of economic analysis?
options: Future amounts are discounted to the present
A positive present worth shows that the project is justified
If the interest rate is not constant, the present worth must be computed in two or more steps
explain: All three statements are correct principles of the present worth method: discounting future amounts, positive PW indicating a justified project, and multi-step computation for variable interest rates.

q: 22. The minimum value of benefit-cost-ratio for the selection of any project should be:
explain: As with earlier questions, the minimum acceptable benefit-cost ratio for project selection is one.

q: 23. The rate on the unrecovered balance of the investment in a situation where the terminal balance is zero:
explain: The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is the interest rate at which the net present value of all the cash flows (both positive and negative) from a project or investment equal zero.

q: 24. In benefit-cost analysis, benefits and costs have to be converted to
explain: Benefits and costs in benefit-cost analysis can be compared using any consistent equivalent worth basis — present, future, or annual worth.

q: 25. Investment less the discounted benefit is called ......
explain: The key marks NPV, the net of discounted benefits against investment.

q: 26. The minimum value of NPV for selection of an Engineering project should be
explain: The minimum acceptable NPV for selecting an engineering project is zero, indicating the project at least breaks even.

q: 27. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as
explain: The current ratio is defined as current assets divided by current liabilities.

q: 28. For a Government funded development project the most important factor to considered is :
explain: Public projects are often driven by social welfare and political objectives rather than pure financial profit.

q: 29. The internal rate of return (IRR) is a rate of return used in capital budgeting to measure and compare the .......... of investments.
explain: IRR measures 'profitability' or 'efficiency'; since these terms aren't in options A, B, or C, 'none of these' is the correct choice.

q: 30. IRR is carried out for
options: evaluation the progress of the project
evaluating the desirability of investment of projects
explain: IRR is a decision-making tool to determine if an investment meets the required return threshold.

q: 31. For selection of any project which of the following is mostly used ......
explain: Key answer d as I read it. Note: this differs from Q29 (IRR) and textbooks usually name NPV or IRR, so please verify against a clearer key.

q: 32. The decession rule for project acceptance is that :
explain: The standard rule is to accept a project if its yield (IRR) is at least equal to the Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR).

q: 33. Which among the following is not true about benefit cost analysis?
options: cost and benefits must be converted to a common time base
a public project is normally acceptable if the B-C ratio is at least one
the analysis makes sure that the benefits are at least 10-20% more than the costs
the B-C ratio is a ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs
explain: There is no universal rule requiring a 10-20% buffer; the basic requirement is simply a ratio of 1.0 or higher.

q: 34. Engineer use flowing techniques while preparing the project appraisal ......
options: rate of return on book value
explain: Discounted cash flow, payback period and rate of return on book value are all appraisal techniques.

q: 35. Project Appraisal means ......
explain: Appraisal means evaluating a proposed option and selecting the best one.

q: 36. Cost benefit study are essential to ......
options: to assess the total cost of work
ascertain the relevant went escalation in prices
evaluate viability and worthwhileness of taking up the project
explain: A cost-benefit study is carried out to decide whether the project is viable and worth undertaking.
